proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 20 contains only a Customer indemnity for "every claim" relating to our use, with no Vendor indemnity at all. We have added the standard Vendor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct/gross negligence, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.

ops.newText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from third-party claims to the extent arising out of content Customer provides to the Services or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
ops.oldText: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, the indemnifying Party shall control the defence, and the indemnified Party shall reasonably cooperate at the indemnifying Party's expense.

proposal.summary: Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity and narrow Customer's indemnity

quote: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
rationale: Section 20 contains only a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity and no Vendor indemnity of any kind — walk-away territory — even though Section 9.3 cross-refers to infringement remedies under "Section 20.5" that do not exist. We added the Vendor IP/breach-of-law/data-breach/wilful-misconduct indemnity with standard procedure and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables
rationale: We own Customer Data and independently developed IP (14.1), Deliverables are assigned to us on creation (14.2), Vendor retains only its pre-existing Vendor Technology but licenses it perpetually via 13.2/14.3, and 14.4 bars joint ownership. Direction of ownership favours us — preferred position met.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved the cap to the greater of twelve months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 and removed "without exception", which otherwise contradicted the Excluded Claims regime in Section 21.3. Our position is that indemnification, confidentiality, data-protection/security and IP-infringement claims sit outside the cap; a one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy.

ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, which are not subject to this limitation, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.

proposal.summary: Raise cap to greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1M and align with Excluded Claims

quote: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
rationale: The cap is mutual and the exclusions/Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3 is exactly our preferred position, but 21.1 sets the cap at one month of Fees actually paid — far below the 6-month walk-away floor and below the 12-month fallback — and "without exception" purports to override the Excluded Claims carve-outs. Redlined to the greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000 and aligned with Section 21.3.

quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: We may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent, Vendor needs our consent (reasonableness qualified) and may never assign to a competitor, and Section 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, repricing or acceleration on our change of control — our preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must keep the freedom to source from other suppliers, so we have deleted the sole-and-exclusive provider obligation in Section 2.2; it also conflicts with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity commitment. If some protection is needed we can discuss a 12-month, single-category exclusivity that ends automatically on any service-level failure.

quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
rationale: Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on us with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory, and it conflicts with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have given no exclusivity commitment. Deleted, with the 12-month/single-category fallback offered if Vendor needs protection.

quote: Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee is payable by Customer anywhere; convenience termination carries no charge (9.4), force-majeure termination is "without penalty" (27.3), and Section 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately not due. The Section 2.1 shortfall exposure is addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than double-counted here.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and excluding our Affiliates and contractors is not usable; we have extended it to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and made revocation subject only to the uncured material breach standard already in Section 13.3.

ops.newText: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a licence, transferable to a successor as permitted by Section 24 and revocable only in accordance with Section 13.3, to use the Services.
ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.

proposal.summary: Extend licence to Affiliates/contractors and remove revocability at will

quote: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
rationale: The subscription grant in 13.1 is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them — the walk-away case. The paid-up grant in 13.2 and the revocation limits in 13.3 do not cure the Services licence itself, so we extended 13.1 to Affiliates and contractors, made it transferable per Section 24, and tied revocation to Section 13.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted Section 12.4; it also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete commitment.

quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
rationale: Section 12.4 imposes a 24-month post-term, worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete on us — squarely walk-away — and contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no non-compete commitment. Deleted; a named-product, in-term restriction with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs is the most we could consider.

quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.
rationale: Section 9.4 gives us a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and no early-termination penalty, and expressly denies Vendor any matching right during a committed term — our preferred position. Section 2.1's take-or-pay language ("without reduction or termination rights") cuts against this and is addressed under MINCOMMIT to avoid double-counting.

quote: Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours
rationale: Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct system access — matches our preferred position.

rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County and no arbitration is our preferred position; the executive-escalation step in Section 28.3 does not delay urgent relief.

rationale: No MFN or best-terms obligation burdens Customer anywhere; the pricing provisions (Sections 7.1 and 8.3) contain no matching or most-favoured-customer mechanic, and Section 12.3 expressly disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment. Meets our preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, particularly as it conflicts with our convenience-termination right in Section 9.4 and Section 12.3. We have narrowed the commitment to the current twelve-month term, reducible on thirty days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.newText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services during the current twelve-month term, which commitment Customer may reduce on thirty days' written notice and which is settled by a true-up of any shortfall rather than a penalty. The commitment does not limit Customer's termination rights under Section 9.
ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.

proposal.summary: Limit take-or-pay to current 12-month term, reducible, with true-up

quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
rationale: Section 2.1 is a three-year, USD 6M take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right — the walk-away case — and it contradicts both our convenience-termination right in Section 9.4 and Section 12.3's disclaimer of any minimum-volume commitment. Narrowed to the fallback: current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up instead of penalty.

rationale: There is no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding Customer anywhere in the document; Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our hiring freedom from general recruitment and disclaims any no-hire commitment. Meets our preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Immediate cessation of assistance and deletion of Customer Data with no export would leave us stranded and contradicts Sections 11.2 and 11.3; we have replaced it with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, with data return and certified deletion following the existing sequence.

ops.newText: On expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including export and migration support, for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, and shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.
ops.oldText: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.

proposal.summary: Replace immediate-deletion clause with transition assistance

quote: Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
rationale: Sections 11.2 and 11.3 give us 30-day data return in machine-readable format and certified deletion, but 11.1 mandates immediate cessation of assistance and immediate permanent deletion with no export — the walk-away case, and internally inconsistent with 11.2/11.3. Replaced 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates and deletion only per 11.2/11.3.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Fifteen days is too short and the "no correction or refund obligation" cut-off would strip the remedy in Section 19.4; we have moved to the market-standard ninety-day Deliverable warranty with the Section 19.4 remedies preserved.

ops.newText: For ninety days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation, and Customer's remedies for nonconformity are as set out in Section 19.4.
ops.oldText: For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.

proposal.summary: Extend Deliverable warranty to 90 days and remove the remedy cut-off

quote: For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
rationale: The workmanlike-manner and conformance warranties in 19.1, the malicious-code/compliance warranty in 19.3 and the repair/replace/refund remedy in 19.4 are strong, but 19.2 caps the Deliverable warranty at 15 days and then strips any correction or refund obligation — below the 30/90-day fallback and it undercuts the 19.4 remedy. Extended to 90 days with the 19.4 remedies preserved.
